reviewdog/action-setup leaked GitHub Actions secrets

Target: reviewdog/action-setup
Date: 2025-03-11 to 2025-03-17 (6 days)
Actor: Unknown attacker (unknown)
Target Kind: ci_cd_plugin
Language: Shell
Cause: compromised_account_credentials
Motive: credential_theft
Transitive: false
Impact: data_exfiltration
User Impact: 1500
Phase: ci_cd
Campaigns: reviewdog and tj-actions leaked CI secrets

Synopsis

Attackers compromised a contributor's Personal Access Token (PAT), traced back to an earlier leak from the SpotBugs project, which granted write access.

Story

The reviewdog/action-setup compromise was the first step in the March 2025 GitHub Actions chain that later exposed `tj-actions/changed-files`. A contributor token leaked earlier through SpotBugs had write access, and the attacker used it against the reviewdog repository.

The attacker moved the `v1` tag to malicious commits. Because GitHub Actions workflows commonly pin actions by tag rather than immutable commit SHA, downstream workflows pulled attacker-controlled code without changing their own repositories.

The malicious action printed CI secrets into logs in a recoverable form. That exposed tokens from projects using the action and supplied the path to compromise `tj-actions/changed-files`, where the same secret-leaking pattern reached a much larger set of repositories.

CISA, NVD, Wiz, StepSecurity, and Unit 42 all treat reviewdog and tj-actions as related supply-chain incidents. This record stays scoped to reviewdog/action-setup; the campaign record carries the two-action chain.
